findings.reason: Verified in scheduleEmailReminders.ts: one try wraps the whole loop, so a SendGrid throw on one reminder skips the rest, and the lazy PrismaPromise deletes never run because the Promise.all is skipped, so rows already cancelled keep cancelled:true and get re-sent on the next run.
This is an unresolved question about SendGrid batch limits that the code cannot answer, and it is phrased as a question, so it is capped low.

The diff confirms deleteScheduledEmailReminder/SMS are called un-awaited in a forEach in handleCancelBooking, replacing an awaited deleteMany, so the cancelled:true update or row delete can be dropped after the response on serverless.

Correct that the sync forEach means the try/catch in handleNewBooking cannot see the async promises, but the inner functions already catch their own errors, so this is dead code and a readability issue only.

Verified that the un-awaited SMS row delete races the cascade delete on workflow and step removal, producing a caught 'Record does not exist' log line but no data loss, so the impact is a misleading log.
Verified with grep that Prisma is unused in workflows.tsx and PrismaPromise is only a type, so the import change is real lint/cleanup debt, with no runtime impact.
